question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Blaze the trail

options.text: Be first to do something important

solution:
The correct answer is "**Be first to do something important".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Blaze the trail"** is an idiom that stemmed from the practice of marking paths through forests with blazed trees.
 
• This idiom usually denotes the actions of an innovator or ground-breaker, someone who establishes a new line of thinking or a new method in a particular field.
 
 
• **Example**- The suffragists blazed a trail, eventually convincing lawmakers to give American women the right to vote.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is **‘Option 4’.**
